system_map.overview: CAS is a CLI-driven continuous architecture system that orchestrates LLM-powered workflows for architecture governance. A central FlowRunner executes sequential steps with a shared context, while governance engine components enforce compliance and a verifier agent provides quality gates. External coding agents are integrated via telemetry adapters.

agents.name: FlowRunner
agents.role: Orchestrates multi-step workflows, passing a mutable context through each step.

agents.name: Verifier
agents.role: Performs quality checks and validation on generated architecture artifacts.

agents.name: GovernanceEngine
agents.role: Evaluates compliance against rules and triggers governance actions based on state transitions.

agents.name: CodingAgents (external)
agents.role: External coding assistants (e.g., Claude Code, Antigravity) that produce architecture code/artifacts.

agents.name: SkillExecutors
agents.role: Execute discrete reusable operations exposed as CLI skills (e.g., add feature, drawio generator).

orchestration.description: FlowRunner acts as a central orchestrator that executes steps sequentially, while governance and verifier agents are invoked as steps or background checks. External coding agents are not directly orchestrated but observed via telemetry.

patterns.name: LLM Provider Abstraction with Mocking

tool_protocols.notes: LiteLLM supports tool calling but system may not use it directly.

optimisation_targets.notes: Abstraction allows switching providers to reduce cost and increase resilience.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Unified interface simplifies agent code while preserving provider flexibility.

patterns.summary: All LLM interactions are routed through a unified client interface, allowing provider portability and deterministic testing via a mock client.
patterns.intent: Decouple agent logic from specific LLM providers to enable switching, cost control, and deterministic testing.
patterns.context: The CAS runner uses LiteLLM for multi-provider support and MockLLMClient for tests.
patterns.solution: Define an LLM client interface; LiteLLMClient wraps LiteLLM, MockLLMClient simulates responses. Runner depends on the interface, not concrete provider.
implementation_signals: Multiple client classes implementing a common interface
Injection of client into runner or steps
patterns.reuse_notes: Use when agent logic should be provider-agnostic; ensure interface covers all needed capabilities.

patterns.name: Pipeline Orchestration with Shared Context

tool_protocols.notes: Steps may invoke LLM via client.

optimisation_targets.notes: Predictable sequence with state passing increases reliability.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Central orchestration keeps steps simple but autonomous.

patterns.summary: Workflows are defined as ordered steps that share a mutable context object, enabling step-by-step orchestration with state propagation.
patterns.intent: Provide a predictable execution model where each step receives and updates the same context.
patterns.context: FlowRunner in runner.py orchestrates steps in a pipeline.
patterns.solution: Define a pipeline of steps, each implementing a prepare_inputs contract; FlowRunner iterates, mutating a shared context.

evidence.note: Central orchestrator; likely executes steps sequentially.

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt for workflows where order matters and state needs to carry across steps; consider immutable context snapshots.

patterns.name: Skill-Based Reusable Capability Modules

tool_protocols.notes: Skills invoked as CLI tools by agents.

optimisation_targets.notes: Reusable skills speed up agent tasks and standardize output.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Skills give agents autonomy to perform complex ops while centralizing definitions.

patterns.summary: Agent capabilities are packaged as discoverable 'skills' (CLI subcommands) that can be invoked by the agent to perform complex, reusable operations.
patterns.intent: Allow agents to perform complex, reusable operations (e.g., add feature, refactor) via standardized skill modules.
patterns.context: Found in .agents/skills and .claude/skills directories with subfolders per skill.
patterns.solution: Define skills as directories with instructions and scripts; agents invoke them as CLI tools.
implementation_signals: Skill directories with SKILL.md or similar
CLI hooks exposing skills as subcommands
patterns.reuse_notes: Use for agent tool extensions; ensure skills are versioned and documented.

patterns.name: Verifier Agent for Quality Gates

tool_protocols.notes: Verifier uses LLM to assess outputs.

optimisation_targets.notes: Dedicated verifier ensures quality before merging.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Separates generation from verification for better quality checks.

patterns.summary: A dedicated verifier agent is used to validate generated architecture artifacts against governance rules and quality criteria before acceptance.
patterns.intent: Add an independent quality gate to catch errors or non-compliance in agent-generated outputs.
patterns.context: Verifier agent defined in both .claude and .agents; likely invoked after main agent produces artifacts.
patterns.solution: Define a verifier agent that takes generated artifacts and rules, returns pass/fail with feedback. Invoked as a step or CI gate.
patterns.reuse_notes: Use as a separate step when accuracy is critical; tune verifier prompts carefully.

patterns.name: Compliance Enforcement via Rule Engine

tool_protocols.notes: Rule engine checks outputs against predefined rules.

optimisation_targets.notes: Enforces governance rules to prevent non-compliance.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Declarative rules limit agent autonomy for safety.

patterns.summary: Compliance is enforced by a rule engine that evaluates agent outputs against governance rules and produces findings.
patterns.intent: Automatically check agent-generated artifacts for compliance with organizational architecture rules.
patterns.context: ComplianceEngine in governance module; likely used by FlowRunner or CI.
patterns.solution: Define compliance rules; engine runs checks against context or artifacts, returning findings and metrics.
patterns.reuse_notes: Use for any system needing rule-based validation of agent outputs.

patterns.name: Governance Action Engine with State Transitions
patterns.summary: Governance actions are determined by a state machine with a transition registry, ensuring only valid transitions trigger actions.
patterns.intent: Provide a structured way to decide and execute governance actions based on current state and allowed transitions.
patterns.context: GovernanceActionEngine uses TransitionRegistry to map state changes to actions.
patterns.solution: Define TransitionRegistry with valid state transitions; engine consults it to produce actions.
patterns.reuse_notes: Use when governance workflows have clear states; keep transition table maintainable.

patterns.name: Telemetry Normalization Adapters
patterns.summary: Telemetry from various external coding agents is normalized into a unified format via adapter classes, enabling consistent monitoring and cost estimation.
patterns.intent: Provide a consistent view of agent activity across different coding tools (Claude Code, Antigravity) for monitoring and governance.
patterns.context: AgentTelemetryAdapter subclasses implement parsing for specific tools.
patterns.solution: Define base adapter class; each coding agent has a subclass (CodingAgentTelemetryAdapter, ClaudeCodeTelemetryAdapter, AntigravityTelemetryAdapter).
patterns.reuse_notes: Use when integrating multiple external agents; keep adapters thin and well-tested.

patterns.name: Template-Driven Knowledge Artifacts

tool_protocols.notes: Agents use templates to produce structured knowledge.

patterns.summary: Architecture knowledge artifacts (ADRs, patterns, signals) are generated using standardized templates to ensure consistency and completeness.
patterns.intent: Simplify creation and maintenance of architecture knowledge by providing reusable templates.
patterns.context: Templates exist for various artifact types (ADR, pattern, signal, learning).
patterns.solution: Define markdown templates for each artifact type; agents and humans fill them out.
patterns.reuse_notes: Use template-driven generation for any structured knowledge output.

patterns.name: Configuration-Driven Execution Context
patterns.summary: Execution parameters such as runtime profile and rule context are externalized in YAML/JSON files, allowing environment-specific behavior without code changes.
patterns.intent: Separate execution configuration from agent logic to allow tuning and environment adaptation.
patterns.solution: Load execution profile and rule context at startup; use them to parameterize runner and governance.
patterns.reuse_notes: Use configuration files for any agentic system needing environment-specific settings.

patterns.name: Pipeline Definition Validation

tool_protocols.notes: Static validation of workflow definitions before use.

patterns.summary: CI/CD workflow files are statically validated to catch syntax errors, hardcoded variables, or anti-patterns before deployment.
patterns.intent: Ensure that workflow definitions are syntactically correct and follow project conventions.
patterns.context: A validation script checks YAML syntax, hardcoding, pinned installers, and other workflow properties.
patterns.solution: Write a Python script that parses workflow YAMLs and applies a set of checks (e.g., check_zero_hardcoding).
patterns.reuse_notes: Use static validation for any pipeline definitions to enforce project conventions.

anti_patterns.name: Skill Duplication Across Agent Configurations
symptoms: Same skill listed in both .agents and .claude directories
Potential for divergent behavior if edited separately
impact: Inconsistent agent behavior depending on environment
Maintenance burden keeping two copies in sync
suggested_remediation: Use a single source of truth (e.g., symlinks or shared repository)
Add CI check to detect duplication or drift
